title: Explosion at Al-Ahli Arab Hospital in Gaza City
body:
On 17 October 2023, at about 7 p.m. local time, an explosion struck the courtyard and parking lot of Al-Ahli Arab Hospital in the Zeitoun neighbourhood of Gaza City, where many displaced Palestinians were sheltering. The Gaza Health Ministry reported that 471 people were killed. Early international reports of more than 500 dead came from a mistranslation that included the injured.

Other estimates were lower. United States intelligence assessed that between 100 and 300 people were killed, with the true figure likely at the low end of that range. The Anglican Diocese of Jerusalem, which manages the hospital, put the toll at about 200, and the director of Al-Shifa Hospital, Mohammed Abu Selmia, said about 250. Human Rights Watch noted that the ministry's figures implied an unusually high ratio of deaths to injuries. None of the figures has been independently verified.

The cause was disputed. Hamas and Palestinian Islamic Jihad blamed an Israeli airstrike. Israel said the blast was caused by a failed rocket launch by Palestinian Islamic Jihad. The United States, France, the United Kingdom and Canada said their intelligence pointed to a misfired Palestinian rocket. Human Rights Watch said in November 2023 that an Israeli airstrike was highly unlikely, while Forensic Architecture reached different conclusions and questioned the rocket explanation. The cause has not been conclusively established. The blast led Jordan to cancel a planned summit with US President Joe Biden.
